title: Freezing & Fine-Tuning Strategies ❄️
description: Decide which layers to freeze and which to train, and set different learning rates.

slides.title: How to Freeze Layers 🧊
slides.content:
# `requires_grad = False`

To freeze a layer, set its parameter's `requires_grad` to `False`. The optimizer will skip them.

```python
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
# Then unfreeze the new head
for param in model.fc.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = True
```

slides.title: Feature Extraction Setup
slides.content: Freeze all parameters except the new fc.
slides.codeSnippet:
model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, 10)
# New fc has requires_grad=True by default
print(model.fc.weight.requires_grad)  # True

quizData.question: After setting `param.requires_grad=False`, what happens during `backward()`?

options.text: Gradients are computed but not applied
No gradients are computed for that parameter
The parameter is set to zero

quizData.explanation: `requires_grad=False` excludes the parameter from the computation graph, saving memory and time.

slides.title: Fine‑Tuning: Unfreeze Some Layers 🔓
slides.content:
## Gradual Unfreezing

Instead of training only the head, we can unfreeze some of the later layers (e.g., the last convolutional block) and train them with a very low learning rate.

This allows the pretrained features to **adapt** slightly to the new domain.

slides.title: Selective Unfreezing
slides.content: Unfreeze only the last ResNet block (layer4).

slides.title: Different Learning Rates 🎚️
slides.content:
## Fine‑Tuning Learning Rate

When unfreezing pretrained layers, use a **lower learning rate** (e.g., 1e-4) than for the new head (1e-3). This prevents destroying the valuable pretrained features.

In PyTorch, you can pass different parameter groups to the optimizer:

```python
optimizer = optim.Adam([
    {'params': model.fc.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-3},
    {'params': model.layer4.parameters(), 'lr': 1e-4}
])
```

slides.title: Differential Learning Rates
slides.content: Apply separate learning rates to head and backbone.

quizData.question: Why use a lower learning rate for pretrained layers?

options.text: To avoid overwriting useful features with large updates

quizData.explanation: Pretrained weights are already good; aggressive updates can erase their knowledge.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Monitor Validation

Always validate when fine‑tuning. If the loss spikes or accuracy drops, lower the learning rate or freeze more layers.
